pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 21-23-25-302-016 (External Patch Repair - Fiberglass or Kevlar Duct).
resposta:
(1) This procedure gives instructions for the repair of a crack or cut in a fiberglass or Kevlar air
 conditioning duct with an external patch.
 (2) An external patch is applicable when the cut or the crack is less than 1/4 inch wide and is less
 than 3 inches long.
 (3) This task includes steps to install insulation material on the air duct.
 (4) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
 replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
 Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
 (5) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged. Replacement
 insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
 (6) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, is the preferred foam insulation material that
 meets the flame propagation requirement.
 (7) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam insulation, G02470 must be wrapped with tape,
 G50327 to meet the flammability/flame propagation requirements. Wrap the tape, G50327
 across 100% of the brown hypalon insulation surface on the polyimide foam insulation,
 G02470.
 (8) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation

resposta:
(1) This inspection procedure is to be done when liquid has been spilled in the galley area.
 NOTE: When a small amount of liquid is spilled, an inspection is not usually necessary.
 (2) In the galley areas, a water (liquid) barrier is installed to contain liquid when it is spilled. To
 protect the water barrier, vinyl mats cover the galley floor.
 (3) In the adjacent entry and service door thresholds, waste water drains are installed to remove
 liquids (gray water) from the floor.
 These drain holes must be kept free from blockages.
 (4) The integrity of the water barrier seal, in the forward galley areas, is most important because
 the location of the electronic equipment compartment is directly below the forward galley.
 (5) A leak from the forward galley which has a damaged water barrier, into the compartment
 below, could possibly cause serious damage to the electronic equipment. The result could be a
 possible hazard to the flight safety of the airplane.
 (6) In all areas where gray water contamination has to be removed and cleaned, you must use an
 approved disinfectant to kill all harmful micro-organisms.

resposta:

 honeycomb cells of the acoustic panels.
 Follow the steps below to minimize the ingestion of cleaning solutions and water into the
 acoustic panels.

 CAUTION: WATER AND CLEANING AGENTS TRAPPED INSIDE THE PANEL WILL LEAD
 TO CORROSION OF THE ALUMINUM HONEYCOMB CORE.
 (a) Wipe cleaning solutions on with a clean cloth, damp, but not saturated, with cleaning
 solution.
 (b) Wipe with a clean cloth, damp with water, to remove all residues.
 (c) Wipe using a clean dry cloth to remove all moisture.
 (2) Use ONLY cleaning agents certified to the requirements of Document D6-17487, Evaluation of
 Airplane Maintenance Materials, when cleaning acoustic panels.
 CAUTION: DO NOT SUBJECT AREAS CONTAINING PERFORATED SKINS TO HIGH
 PRESSURE SPRAYING, OR SUBMERGE IN SOLVENTS OR WATER.
 (3) If pressure washing is required for components around acoustic panels, the acoustic portion of
 the nacelle should be covered to prevent ingestion of the cleaning solutions.

 such as Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Tri

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-51-57-200-801 (Volcanic Ash Ground Fallout Conditional Inspection).
resposta:
(1) This task has information to examine a parked airplane for contamination in volcanic ash fallout
 conditions.
 (2) Fallout is identified as ash drifting down from the air, or is blown about by the wind. Fallout is
 also caused by the ash being blown or moved about because of the movement of airplanes
 and ramp vehicles.
 (3) For airplanes parked in fallout conditions, protect all inlets of systems, probes, static ports,
 engines, gaps, etc. with suitable covers.
 (a) Any covered areas should have appropriate streamers or markings, to be removed
 before operation.
 (4) Volcanic ash has the qualities that follow:
 (a) It is hard and highly abrasive.
 (b) It usually contains trace chemicals which can be acidic (pH between 2 and neutral).
 (c) It can cause erosion/abrasion, etching or shot peening on exposed surfaces and remove
 protective finishes.
 (d) The dimensions of most ash particles are less than 5 microns with trace amounts that are
 more than 50 microns.
 (e) It resembles talcum powder.
 (f) It stays on exposed lubricated surfaces.
 (g) Able to enter small orifices and pass by seals.
 (h) Can cause unusual wear and contamination of many airplane systems and filter
 elemen

 (PAGEBLOCK 51-21-31/701).

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 12-33-02-603-024 (Cold Weather Unattended Parking at Temperatures Below 32F (0C)).
resposta:
(1) This task is to park the airplane during cold weather in an unattended parking condition.
 Unattended parking is generally used when the airplane will be on the ground in a
 non-operational condition between flights.
 (2) During unattended parking, the temperatures of the cabin and flight deck are not maintained
 warmer than 32°F (0°C) and the engines are not maintained warmer than -40°F (-40°C) while
 the airplane is on the ground.
 (3) For airplanes that operate continuously in cold weather, put the airplane into a heated hangar
 periodically to thaw the insulation blankets and other equipment.
 (4) If the temperature of the fuel is below 32°F (0°C), do not to drain the fuel tank sumps. To check
 for water at the fuel tank sump drain valves with fuel temperature below 32°F (0°C), do this
 task to raise the temperature of the fuel: Fuel Sump Drainage, TASK 12-11-01-683-103-001.
 (5) When adding fuel, you must use these requirements:
 (a) Make sure the fuel temperature is at least 6°F or 3°C above the fuel freeze point. Use the
 ASTM method to determine the freeze point.
 NOTE: The Fuel Quantity Indicator on the wing fuel station can indicate slowly or not
 show numbers in cold

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-11-00-208-199 (Fuel Leak Analysis to Find the Cause of the Leaks).
resposta:
(1) These are the causes of most of the leaks in the fuel tank structure:
 (a) Surfaces are prepared incorrectly.
 (b) Sealants are mixed or kept incorrectly.
 (c) Sealants are applied incorrectly.
 (d) Fasteners are loose.
 (e) The fittings or the connections are installed incorrectly.
 (2) This task gives data about the causes of fuel leaks. It also gives general precautions that you
 must obey when you repair leaks.
SUBTASK 28-11-00-288-200

 (1) The surfaces are prepared incorrectly.
 (a) The surfaces must not contain these unwanted materials:
 1) Grease
 2) Metal particles
 3) Hair
 4) Loose paint
 5) Wax
 6) Other unwanted materials.
 (b) These unwanted materials can cause the sealant not to bond correctly.
 SUBTASK 28-11-00-288-239

 (2) The sealants are mixed or kept incorrectly.
 (a) Make sure you mix the correct quantities of the base material and the accelerator
 material.
 NOTE: Sealants have two parts that you must mix together, the base material and the
 accelerator material. Synthetic rubber makes the base for most sealants. The
 manufacturer adds materials to control the strength and cure time. The
 manufacturer also adds materials to make the sealant more flexible

 adjustment procedure.

 (1) Do a visual check of the metal areas on the N1 speed sensor for this type of damage:
 (a) Cracks
 1) No cracks are permitted.

 1) Replace the N1 speed sensor if the damage is not in the limits.
 (c) Mount flange that is not flat by more than 0.04 inch (1 mm).
 1) Replace the N1 speed sensor if the damage is not in the limits.
 SUBTASK 77-12-01-212-009-C00

 (2) Do a visual check of the electrical connector on the N1 speed sensor for this type of damage:
 (a) More than full thread damage on 30% of one entrance thread or 20% of two entrance
 threads or crossed threads
 1) Chase the threads if the damage is in the limits.
 2) Replace the N1 speed sensor if the damage is not in the limits.
 (b) Pins that do not engage freely with the connector
 1) Make the bent pins straight.
 2) Replace the N1 speed sensor if the pins are broken, have erosion or do not engage
 easily.
 (c) Dirt in the connector
 1) Clean the N1 speed sensor.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-00-00-202-017 (Inspection of the Electrical Bonding Jumpers in the Fuel System).
resposta:
(1) This task contains visual and mechanical inspections of the electrical bonding jumpers in the
 fuel system.
 (2) Do not flex, bend or kink the bonding jumpers more than is necessary. If the bonding jumpers
 are moved too much, it can cause the loss of tin plating on the wire braid of the bonding
 jumper.
 (3) When you inspect the bonding jumpers you may see black or brown deposits on the wire braid.
 This can occur when there is a deterioration of the tin plating on the bonding jumper and the
 copper in the wire reacts with the sulfur compounds. This discoloration is not a problem unless
 the wire braid contains broken strands. If the bonding jumper has broken strands, then you
 must replace the bonding jumper.
 (4) When you inspect the bonding jumpers, inspect for loose clamps and corrosion.

 center tank to the two wing tanks. If the fuel level in the center tank is higher than the fuel level

 scavenge system. Thus, the gate assembly must be replaced before the fuel level in the No. 1
 tank rises to the level of the fuel crossfeed valve.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 21-23-25-212-193 (Insulation Repair - Ducts Wrapped with Foam Insulation).
resposta:
(1) This procedure gives instructions to repair cuts or tears in the insulation on air conditioning
 ducts wrapped with foam insulation.
 (2) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
 replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
 14 Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
 (a) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged.
 Replacement insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
 (b) Melamine foam, BMS8-385, is the preferred insulation material that meets the flame
 propagation requirement.
 (c) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in
 flammability properties over time.
 (d) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, existing tape that does not meet
 the flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that
 does meet the requirement.
 (e) BMS5-157 is the preferred tape material that meets the flame propagation requirement.
 (f) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam, BMS8-300, must be wrapped with tape,
 BMS5-157, to meet the flammability/flame prop

resposta:
(1) Autoslat system components used in this test are the No. 1 and No. 2 Autoslat Computers
 (ASC), the Angle of Airflow (AOA) Sensors, and the antiskid control unit.
 (2) The Stall Warning system is activated when the angle of attack increases to cause a stall
 warning to appear at the stick shakers.
 The AOA trip angle changes with airspeed, flap position and if the airplane is near the ground.
 These different trip angles are calculated by the stall warning computer.
 (3) All angle of airflow vane angles used in this test are referenced to the angle of airflow test
 fixture protractor. The angle of airflow vane angles given must be corrected for each individual
 vane offset.
 The vane offset is stamped on the trailing edge of each angle of airflow vane. When testing the
 left angle of airflow vane, the vane offset must be added to the test angle requirements; when
 testing the right vane, the vane offset must be subtracted from the test angle requirements.
 (4) The sign convention for the AOA vane angles specified in this test is the same for the left and
 the right AOA sensor vanes. On the calibrator tool, the numbers below the zero point of the
 main scale are positive degrees

 these alternatives.
 (2) Use the applicable consumable materials that are necessary for the repair procedure you use.
SUBTASK 25-52-60-348-068

 (1) Get the correct Thermion patch kit for the shape of the damage.
 NOTE: The patch should make a minimum of a 2-inch overlap on the area that is not
 damaged. For example, the patch dimension that is necessary for a 1.5-inch diameter
 hole would be 5.5-inch diameter.
 SUBTASK 25-52-60-128-069

 (2) Rub the back of the patch with abrasive paper to remove the gloss being careful not to rub the
 impregnated scrim area.
 SUBTASK 25-52-60-128-070

 (3) Use the abrasive paper to remove all signs of the tedlar on the area of the liner to be contacted
 by the patch.
 NOTE: Tedlar is a protective white layer that is on the liner during the manufacture process.
 SUBTASK 25-52-60-168-071

 (4) Clean all of the surfaces using denatured alcohol to remove the loose particles.
 SUBTASK 25-52-60-348-072

 (5) Apply epoxy to the back of the patch and to the liner.

resposta:
(1) Corrosion evaluation will be required after initial inspection and cleaning to determine the
 nature and extent of the repair or rework.
 It is difficult to establish a distinct and specific dividing line between various conditions.
 Consequently, the first requirement for evaluation is a good, and sound, maintenance
 judgment.
 B. Evaluate any corrosion as follows:
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-017

 (1) LIGHT CORROSION - Characterized by a discoloration or pitting of the surface to a depth of
 approximately 0.001 inch (0.025 mm) maximum.
 This type of damage will normally be removed by a light hand sanding or a minimal chemical
 treatment.
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-018

 (2) MODERATE CORROSION - This corrosion appears similar to LIGHT CORROSION except
 that there may be some blistering, or evidence of scaling and flaking. Pitting depths may be as
 deep as 0.010 inch (0.254 mm). This type of corrosion damage will normally be removed by
 extensive hand or mechanical sanding.
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-019

 (3) HEAVY (SEVERE) CORROSION - The general appearance may be similar to MODERATE
 CORROSION with severe blistering, exfoliation and scaling or flaking. Pitting depths will be
 deeper than 0.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-51-60-200-801 (Extreme High Wind Event - Conditional Inspection).
resposta:
(1) This procedure has information for an aircraft that has had an extreme high wind event while
 parked.
 (a) Examples of extreme high wind events are tornadoes and microbursts.
 (b) Examples of evidence of an extreme high wind event are if the airplane moved over the
 chocks or if there are tire skid marks on the ground where the airplane was parked. This
 may indicate that the airplane has moved from the position in which it was originally
 parked.
 1) If the airplane has moved over wheel chocks, it can cause damage to the tires,
 wheels, and landing gear.
 (2) Extreme high wind events are variable and unpredictable.
 (3) Extreme high winds from the side and aft direction while parked can cause damage to the
 aircraft flight control surfaces and flight control mechanisms internal to the wings, horizontal
 stabilizer, and vertical stabilizer. It is possible that this damage will not be seen during a
 walk-around or during pre-flight checks. The integrity of the flight controls is very important to
 the safe flight of the airplane.
 (4) When the conditional inspection tells you to “examine” a component, look for these damage
 conditions:
 • Cracks

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-11-00-796-063 (Alternative Procedures for Fuel Tank Leak Detection).
resposta:
(1) The best leak detection procedure is usually to find the leak externally with talcum powder and
 then to find the internal leak with the air pressure and soap bubble procedure ("backblowing").
 That procedure is given in the above task: Leak Detection and Repair.
 (2) This task contains alternative procedures used to find a leak. These procedures can be used if
 backblowing is not possible, or if it fails to show all of the leaks. This task also contains the
 internal pressure and bubble procedure which can be used to find external leak locations after
 an airplane is defueled. These are the procedures:
 (a) Pressure Box Application
 (b) Dye Injection Procedure
 (c) Internal Pressure and Bubble Procedure
 (d) The hollow bolt procedure (for use in areas of complex structure)
 (e) The hollow bolt and dye injection procedure.
 (3) Before you defuel a fuel tank which has a leak, try to find all of the leaks in the fuel tank.
 Repair all leaks each time a fuel tank is defueled to repair leaks.
NOTE: To do this procedure, you use a leak tracing device (Figure 613) to put fuel colored with dye
 through the external leak point to the leak source in the tank.
 SUBTASK 28-11-00-286-076

resposta:

 ATC - Operational Test, then it uses ground test equipment to examine the left and right ATC
 systems.
 (2) The ATC-601 can test ATCRBS Mode A, Mode C and Mode S transponders. ATC-601 test sets
 with software version 3.0 or higher can also test Mode S Transponders with Enhanced
 Surveillance (ELS, EHS and ES) capabilities.
 (3) The ATC-601 Series ramp test set, COM-4113 test set uses thirty-nine (39) different tests to
 check the functionality of the ATC transponder. All thirty-nine (39) tests can be run
 automatically in the AUTO mode, or individually in the single test mode.
 (4) In the AUTO mode, the test set will determine the correct set of tests, either Mode A/C or Mode
 S upon receiving the transponder RF signal, and will automatically run the tests.
 (5) The details of individual tests conducted during the AUTO TEST are stored in memory and
 may be reviewed by using the SELECT keys. The PASSED/FAILED indication is shown on top
 of the page.
 (6) A passed Auto Test complies with the FAR Part 43 Appendix F test requirements.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 32-41-54-704-014 (Test the Brake Accumulator Pressure Gage).
resposta:
SUBTASK 32-41-54-714-013

 (1) To test the brake accumulator pressure gage, do the steps that follow:
 (a) Make sure that there is no power to hydraulic systems A and B. If they have power, do
 this task (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-00/201).
 (b) Make sure the pressure gage shows approximately 3000 psi.
 (c) Fully push the captain's brake pedal twelve times to remove the hydraulic pressure from
 the brake accumulator.
 (d) Make sure that the pressure gage shows approximately 1000 psi.
 NOTE: The correct precharge pressure for the brake accumulator is shown on a placard
 near the pressure gage.

 WARNING: KEEP PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT CLEAR OF THE FLIGHT CONTROL
 SURFACES, THE THRUST REVERSERS, AND THE LANDING GEAR. THESE
 COMPONENTS CAN MOVE SUDDENLY WHEN YOU SUPPLY HYDRAULIC
 POWER. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO
 EQUIPMENT.
 (e) Pressurize hydraulic systems A and B (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-00/201).
 (f) Make sure the pressure gage shows approximately 3000 psi.
 (g) Remove the power from hydraulic systems A and B (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-00/201).

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 20-10-27-912-001 (Use of Heat Guns, Soldering Guns, and Soldering Irons).
resposta:
(1) This procedure gives the minimum recommended safety procedures for heat guns, soldering
 guns, and soldering irons used near airplanes.
 These are general procedures. If regulations made by local agencies or procedures made by
 the airline are more applicable, use them.
 Boeing cannot know or write about all possible conditions which the airlines can have.
 (2) You must examine the conditions and be careful. Customer airlines must know how heat guns,
 soldering guns, and soldering irons are used.
 (3) Heat guns, soldering guns, and soldering irons can cause an explosion. Components in all of
 these devices can operate at temperatures higher than the fuel ignition temperature (450°F).
 Heat guns and soldering guns also can contain electrical switches which can cause sparks.
 These sparks can cause the fuel to burn.
 (4) We do not recommend you use a device to supply heat in the fuel tanks. You can have a good
 flow of air in the fuel tanks. You can make them safe when you fill the fuel tanks with nitrogen.
 For the repair of the wires in the fuel tanks, we recommend you use procedures that use
 crimped splices and sleeves with nylon ties.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-00-53-211-803 (Corrosion Prevention - Lower Lobe Interior Structure -- Forward).
resposta:
SUBTASK 05-00-53-211-003

 (1) Remove forward cargo compartment floor panels and check bilge areas under forward cargo
 compartment between stringers 25 L and R for corrosion (CPM 53-10-37 Volume 2, Figure 2).
 SUBTASK 05-00-53-902-001

 (2) Remove corrosion, replace broken or damaged finishes and accomplish repairs to fuselage
 structure as necessary (CPM 53-10-37 Volume 2, Figure 1).
 SUBTASK 05-00-53-916-006

 (3) Apply corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 to all exposed lower lobe structure including
 skin, floor beams, frames, stringers and bulkheads. Pay particular attention to the spraying of
 corrosion inhibiting compound, G00009 on lap joints, rivet heads and stringers below the cargo
 compartment flooring (CPM 20-60-00 Volume 1, CPM 53-10-37 Volume 2, Figure 2).
 NOTE: Allow the compound sufficient time to dry on the lower lobe structure before reinstalling
 the insulation blankets. Ensure that the blankets are not wetted with corrosion
 inhibiting compound, G00009 to preclude potential fire hazards.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 38-32-00-705-119 (Service Panel Drain Valve Leak Test).
resposta:
(1) This procedure tests the service panel drain valve for leakage. Repeat this procedure as
 required to test additional service panel drain valves.
SUBTASK 38-32-00-615-241

 CAUTION: DO NOT USE A TOILET SERVICE LINE PRESSURE OF MORE THAN 60 PSIG (414
 KPA). MORE THAN 60 PSIG (414 KPA) LINE PRESSURE CAN POSSIBLY CAUSE
 EQUIPMENT DAMAGE AND LEAKS.
 (1) Do the servicing procedure for the toilet tank but drain the chemical precharge after five
 minutes (PAGEBLOCK 12-17-00/301).
 NOTE: The recommended toilet service line pressure is 20-50 psig (138-345 kPa). The
 maximum pressure is 60 psig (414 kPa). If the rinse pressure is less than 20 psig (138
 kPa) the waste tank will not get clean.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 32-41-00-802-001 (Bleed the Hydraulic Brake System).
resposta:
(1) The brake hydraulic system must be bled when a hydraulic line of the brake system is opened
 or if a component connected to the system is replaced. When the system is bled, the air in the
 brake lines or a component of the brake system is transmitted to the reservoir by the return
 lines or released to the atmosphere.
 (2) The quantity of time to bleed the system will be kept to a minimum if the brakes are filled and
 bled on the bench.
 (3) There are two tests in this task: one for the Normal Brake System and one for the Alternate
 Brake System.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 32-00-03-206-001 (Inspection for Cracking and Chipping on the Shock Strut Inner Cylinder Chrome).
resposta:
SUBTASK 32-00-03-416-002

 WARNING: YOU MUST CAREFULLY INSTALL THE GROUND LOCKS IN ALL LANDING GEAR.
 AN ACCIDENTAL RETRACTION OF THE LANDING GEAR CAN CAUSE INJURY TO
 PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
 (1) Make sure the ground locks are installed in all the landing gear (PAGEBLOCK 32-00-01/201).
 SUBTASK 32-00-03-566-003

 (2) Look for damage of the scraper ring, and shock strut seals.
 (a) Look at the chrome surface of the inner cylinder before you clean it.
 NOTE: If you see vertical streaks of fluid or contamination on the chrome surface, it is an
 indication that the scraper ring is worn.
 (b) Make sure that the scraper ring is in the installed position.
 NOTE: During operation, the scraper ring moves down the inner cylinder. A mirror and
 flashlight can help you see the scraper ring. Put the mirror below the outer
 cylinder and against the inner cylinder to see the condition and position of the
 scraper ring.
 (c) If you find a problem with the scraper ring, do these steps:
 1) Look for leakage from the shock strut seal.
 2) Deflate the strut and drain the oil.
 3) Disconnect the gland nut from the outer cylinder, then lower the gland nut until you
 can see the scraper ring.

 opposite reverser half is the left reverser half on the No. 1 engine.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 27-09-71-825-036 (Trailing Edge Flaps for 15-Unit Discrepancy Adjustment).
resposta:
(1) Before you adjust the trailing edge flaps, these checks must be satisfactory with the flaps in the
 up position:
 (a) The angular clearance between the upstops on the ballscrew yoke and the ballscrew nut
 must be 170 to 190 degrees (1/2 turn ±10 degrees) turn. If you made trim correction, the
 angular clearance can be 1/4 to 5/6 turn.
 (b) Adjustment of the flap transmissions is necessary if the angular clearance is more than
 the specified limits.
 (2) These checks must be satisfactory with the flaps in the 40-unit detent:
 (a) The clearances between the midflap trailing edge to the aftflap leading edge for the
 inboard ends (of the left and right flaps) and outboard ends (of the left and right flaps)
 must be equal.
 A tolerance of 0.05 inch is permitted.
 (b) Adjustment of the aftflap bellcrank clevis arm is necessary if the left and right flap
 clearances are not equal.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-11-00-368-295 (Temporary Repair of Leaks Through Self-Sealing Rivets).
resposta:
(1) Self-sealing rivets are frequently used in skin panels in the fuel tank area. If you find a leak at a
 rivet, you must replace the rivet to make a permanent repair. You can make a temporary repair
 if you refer to the Structural Repair Manual to make a permanent repair when you go into the
 tank.
 (2) To make a temporary repair of a self-sealing rivet, use one of these procedures:
 (a) Apply the sealant to a self-sealing rivet with a sealant tool (Figure 816).
 (b) Apply the sealant to a self-sealing rivet with a fuel tank rivet sealing tool, SPL-1762
 (Figure 815).

RAM ALL 28-11-00

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (c) Install a Click-Patch.
 (3) For applying sealants in the fuel tank structure(s), it is acceptable to use sealant, A50303, as
 an alternative to sealant, A00767, for Class A and B applications:
 (a) sealant, A50153, can be used as an alternative to sealant, A50301.
 (b) sealant, A50110, can be used as an alternative to sealant, A50302.
 (c) sealant, A50153, cannot be used in combination with sealant, A50302, and sealant,
 A50301, cannot be used with sealant, A50110.

resposta:
(1) This procedure gives instructions to replace the insulation on air conditioning ducts that are
 wrapped with foam insulation.
 (2) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
 replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
 14 Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
 (a) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged.
 Replacement insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
 (b) Melamine foam, BMS8-385, is the preferred insulation material that meets the flame
 propagation requirement.
 (c) Do not use BMS8-39 polyurethane foam insulation for repairs due to the degradation in
 flammability properties over time.
 (d) When insulation material is removed and re-installed, existing tape that does not meet
 the flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that
 does meet the requirement.
 (e) BMS5-157 is the preferred tape material that meets the flame propagation requirement.
 (f) Air conditioning ducts with polyimide foam, BMS8-300, must be wrapped with tape,
 BMS5-157, to meet the flammability/flame propagation

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 20-10-51-308-274 (Repair Size 16 (1 inch) and Size 20 (1-1/4 inch) 6061-T4 Aluminum Tubing in the Hydraulic System).
resposta:
WARNING: DO NOT USE THIS PROCEDURE ON OXYGEN TUBING. GREASE, DIRT, OR
 OTHER FLAMMABLE MATERIALS IN THE OXYGEN TUBING CAN CAUSE A FIRE
 OR EXPLOSION.
 (1) The hydraulic system in the airplane contains both 6061-T4 and T6 aluminum tubes.
 (2) This is a repair method that applies only to 6061-T4 hydraulic aluminum tubes in Sizes 16 (1
 inch) and 20 (1-1/4 inch) and uses 6061–T6 aluminum tube material for making a splice.
 6061-T6 material may be used as an alternate material for repair of 6061-T4 aluminum tubes,
 but 6061-T4 aluminum tube material may NOT be used to repair 6061-T6 aluminum tubes.
 (3) Approved repairs to 6061-T6 aluminum hydraulic tube material are covered elsewhere in this
 AMM.
 (4) Repair is accomplished using only the BACS13BX sleeve, the elastomer swaging process, and
 other applicable methods specified in this procedure for flareless tube repairs.
 (5) The wear depth limit for 6061-T4 tubes is 1/3 the wall thickness of the tube.

 1) The oxygen must contain no less than 99.5% oxygen by volume.
 2) The oxygen must be free from all poisonous contamination to the maximum
 possible level.
 3) The moisture content must not be more than 0.02 milligrams of water vapor for each
 liter of gas at a temperature of 70 degrees Fahrenheit and a pressure of 760
 millimeters of mercury.
 a) Refer to S.A.E. (AS 1065A) for the permitted moisture quantity.
 4) Oxygen of specification MIL-0-27210 of Type 1 agrees with these requirements and
 is recommended.
 (3) Precaution Data
 (a) Make sure that your hands, clothing, tools, area, and equipment are clean and free of
 petroleum materials.
 (b) Keep the oxygen away from ignition sources (heat, sparks and flame) and other material
 that can cause an ignition.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 34-53-02-735-255 (System Test - ATC System (With the TIC T-48 or T-49 Test Set)).
resposta:
(1) This system test is a more complete check of the ATC system. The system test first does the
 ATC - Operational Test. Then it uses ground test equipment to examine the left and right ATC
 systems.
 (2) This system test uses the T-48/-49 ramp test set, COM-10730 to test the functionality of the
 ATC transponder. The test set can do all the tests automatically or each test individually. Each
 test shows on the test set as it is done. If a test has failed, the test sequence will stop and a
 failed message shows. All data will show at the end of the test if the test is successful.
 (3) Operation with the antenna coupler, TAP-115, TAP 118, or TAP 125 used with the applicable
 test set, is necessary when the test to do a check of the output power, receiver, sensitivity and
 radio frequency. For mode S diversity channel isolation check, the TAP 125 is necessary.

resposta:
(1) The chemicals used for magnesium treatment are:
 Chromic Acid (Cr03) Calsium Solfate (CaS04.2H20)
 (2) Magnesium alloys are highly susceptible to corrosion when the metal surface is exposed
 without a protective finish. An oxide-carbonate film will normally form on an exposed
 magnesium alloy surface, but this surface provides very little protection against corrosion. A
 proper protective finish is therefore required.
 (3) All magnesium alloy surfaces that have been reworked per PAGEBLOCK 51-00-53/201 will be
 cleaned and treated with a conversion coating.
 The coating materials convert the magnesium alloy surface into an inhibitive passive layer on
 the base metal that resists corrosion.
 This coating is applied using the brush-on method.

 adjustment procedure.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 08-20-00-912-001 (Procedures to Weigh the Airplane).
resposta:
SUBTASK 08-20-00-912-002

 (1) There are three equally accurate procedures to weigh the airplane:
 (a) Landing Gear Wheels with Floor Scales
 (b) Main Landing Gear and Nose Gear Jack Points
 (c) Wing and Aft Body Jack Points
 SUBTASK 08-20-00-912-003

 (2) Determine the procedure to use based on these factors:
 (a) Type of equipment available
 (b) Cost of new equipment
 (c) Projected demand for aircraft to be weighed.
 SUBTASK 08-20-00-912-006

 (3) If floor scales are available, use procedure (a). You can weigh the airplane faster with this
 procedure than with procedures in which jacks are necessary.
 SUBTASK 08-20-00-912-005

 (4) Procedure (b) is better than the procedure that uses wing or body jack points because there is
 less chance of structural damage to the airplane through failure of a support jack or weigh cell.
 SUBTASK 08-20-00-912-004

 (5) Procedure (b) is more economical and faster than procedure (c) because installation of oleo
 locks are not necessary.

 the injection of Mode S signals into the receiver unit to examine if the signals are processed
 properly. If the Mode S function fails, the red TPR FAIL LED indicator comes on.

 (d) Make sure the LEDs sequence that follows occurs:
 1) All LEDs comes on for about one second.
 2) All red LEDs go off.
 3) The green LED stay on.

 system is pressurized. To do the system test, it is necessary to pressurize the NGS with

 sequence test that does a check of the open and closed position of all of the electrically
 controlled valves. This includes the NGS shutoff valve, ram air valve, overtemperature
 shutoff valve and the ASM high-flow valve. The system test also does a test of the filter
 pressure switch and a test for sensor drift for the NGS bleed pressure sensor.

resposta:
(1) Topcoat (BMS 10–102 Type II Componets) shall be applied to all exposed insulative coating
 surfaces.
 (2) Before applying the topcoat, verify that the insulative coating (BMS 10–102 Type I
 Components) to which it is to be applied is fully cured.
SUBTASK 78-31-01-500-003-C00

 (1) Prepare the topcoat application method (Grade A):
 (a) Mix the RTV60 adhesive, A00578 with Hitco F100-A20 silica fiber, G50384.
 1) The quantity of Hitco F100-A20 silica fiber, G50384 added shall be 2.0 to 3.0
 percent by weight.
 2) Mix the fibers into the topcoat until they are uniformly dispersed.
 3) Mix and thin the two items with solvent, B00083
 a) Do not use solvent, B00083 to thin the topcoat if Catalyst B is used.
 SUBTASK 78-31-01-350-002-C00

 (2) Apply the topcoat (Grade A):
 (a) Apply the topcoat to a thickness of 0.003 in. (0.076 mm) to 0.005 in. (0.127 mm).
 1) Brush application is preferred since one coat since one coat will normally provide
 the required thickness.
 2) Apply as uniformly as possible.
 (b) Cure the topcoat to the values shown in Effects Of Catalyst Concentration On Topcoat
 Usage Properties/Table 802.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-11-00-202-001 (Detection Test for Microbial Growth).
resposta:
(1) Use a microbial detection kit or laboratory standard test to check the fuel/water samples taken
 from each fuel tank. A positive result for microbial contamination requires action that may
 include a biocide treatment or physical removal of the growth from the fuel tanks.
 (2) These are the approved microbial test kit, COM-4806:
 (a) FUELSTAT RESINAE
 (b) EASICULT COMBI
 (c) MICROBMONITOR2
 (d) HY-LITE JET A-1 FUEL TEST
 (e) The fuel samples can also be sent to a laboratory for testing. IP385 is the Institute for
 Petroleum's test for microbial contamination.
 (3) All instructions supplied with the detection kits should be followed closely. It is important to
 retest if a detection test shows microbial contamination. Differences in the fuel/water sample
 and the ability of the detection kits to consistently measure the level of microbial growth make it
 important to retest and verify test results. Do not compare the test results between the different
 types of detection kits.
 (4) All time intervals listed in this task are recommendations. There is no MMEL or scheduled
 maintenance requirements for testing for microbial contamination.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 70-20-02-912-002-C00 (Tightening Practices and Torque Values).
resposta:
(1) This procedure has the definitions, terms and procedures that you use to tighten the fasteners
 that have threads (bolts, nuts and fittings).
 (2) When you turn a fastener around the axis of the fastener you cause torque.
 (3) Usually, you will use the torque values that are specified in this procedure.
 (a) When a installation procedure gives you a torque value, use that torque value.
 (b) But when an installation procedure tells you to tighten a bolt, but does not give a torque
 value, refer to 20-50-11/201.
 (4) Make sure that you apply the torque accurately.
 (a) A torque of one pound-inch is a force of one pound applied to a lever at a distance of one
 inch from the of the fastener (whereas one N.m is the force of one Newton you apply to a
 lever one meter in length).
 (b) To calculate the torque, you multiply the force that you apply in pounds (Newtons) by the
 distance of the force from the axis of the fastener in inches (meters).
 (c) The specified torque is the best value for the fastener and the part that it holds. The
 specified torque will cause the fastener to hold the part tightly but will not break the
 fastener or the part.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-51-52-200-801 (Heavy Water Spray from Tires During Takeoff and Landing - Inspection/Check).
resposta:
(1) This procedure has one task:
 (a) This task is to inspect the aircraft exterior when there is possible water damage.
SUBTASK 05-51-52-211-001

 (1) Make sure that the exterior components are attached correctly and are not damaged.
 (a) Examine the areas that follow.
 1) Wing leading edge structure between the fuselage and the engine.
 2) Lower surfaces of the fuselage.
 3) Antenna and water drain masts.
 4) Landing gear doors.
 5) Inboard trailing edge flap panels.
 6) Landing gear hydraulic plumbing.
 a) Make sure that the plumbing is attached correctly.
 b) Look closely at the lower surface of the track.
 7) Electrical conduits.
 8) Switches, switch targets, and mounting brackets.
 9) Temperature sensors and electrical connectors.
 (b) If damage to any of the exterior components is found, see the SRM for repairs.

(1) This procedure flushes the hydraulic system after you replace a defective hydraulic pump.

 case drain hose or quick-disconnect may be required.

 then it is recommended to do these steps:
 NOTE: Operator experience shows that a new filter can become plugged by debris that
 remains in the hydraulic system after a mechanical failure. A plugged filter can cause
 hydraulic fluid to bypass the filter element and allow debris to circulate in the system.
 Debris that bypasses the filter can cause a premature failure of a new hydraulic pump.
 (a) Replace the case drain filter element again, at the first scheduled maintenance
 opportunity following one week of normal operation.
 (b) Replace all the filter elements in the system at the first scheduled maintenance
 opportunity following two months of normal operation.

 14 Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.

 propagation requirement.

 flammability properties over time.

 the flame propagation requirement must be removed or completely covered with tape that
 does meet the requirement.

resposta:
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to do an inspection on the engine vents and drains
 system.
 (2) This task also gives the inspection criteria for fluid leakage from the engine/strut drains and the
 action to stop the leakage if the leakage rates are more than the limits.
 (3) The leakage rates given in the tables are the threshold limits and the servicable limits from
 different engine drain sources and both limits apply to engines that are not operated and
 engines that are operated at all power settings.
 (4) If the leakage rate is more than the serviceable limit, a corrective action is required.
 (5) If the leakage rate is less than the threshold limit, no action is required.
 (6) If the leakage rate is more than the threshold limit, but less than the servicable limit, an engine
 run is recommended to determine whether the leak increases or decreases with an operational
 engine and to verify the leakage source.
 (7) If you find leakage, the amount of the leakage must be measured to find the appropriate

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 51-00-53-102-043 (Corrosion Removal Procedures).
resposta:
(1) Corrosion can be removed by mechanical or chemical procedures. Examples of mechanical
 removal are:
 (a) Hand sanding with an abrasive paper or metal-wool.
 (b) Power sanding or buffing with abrasive pads.
 (c) Grinding wheels and abrasive blasting with compressed air, which includes abrasive
 blasting with glass beads.
 (2) The decision on which method to use is determined by the different types of metals, different
 amounts of corrosion and the ease of access to the area or part.
 (3) In most corrosion removal operations, the mechanical methods are recommended.
 NOTE: The chemicals used in the chemical removal procedures can cause corrosion and
 must not be allowed to flow into joints, seams or on to highly stressed steel parts.
 (4) If the area of corrosion includes or is near fasteners, remove the fasteners before starting to
 remove the corrosion. There could be corrosion under the fastener heads or in the holes.
 Corrosion removal around such fasteners without removing the fasteners will not stop the
 corrosion under the fasteners (Figure 203). Also, metal from the fastener heads will be rubbed
 into the adjacent metal surface during the corrosion removal procedures, and

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-51-14-202-001 (Mercury Spillage Conditional Inspection).
resposta:
SUBTASK 05-51-14-160-001

 (1) A mercury spill must be considered hazardous, and immediate action must be taken to isolate,
 inspect, and clean the aircraft.
 (2) The corrosive action of mercury is very rapid in pitting and intergranular.
 (3) Mercury amalgamates quickly with aluminum alloys at room temperature if the oxide film on
 the aluminum has been scratched or damaged.
 (a) Once a small area of aluminum has been amalgamated, corrosion and liquid metal
 embrittlement occurs. This process is accelerated by moisture and particularly by salt
 water.
 (4) The amalgamation of stressed aluminum structure may also result in rapid cracking similar to
 stress corrosion cracking.
 (5) Mercury is not consumed in the amalgamation process. As the aluminum oxidizes, it separates
 from the amalgam and the mercury continues to attack fresh aluminum.
 (6) The presence of organic finishes, greases or a thick continuous oxide layer retards the
 amalgamation process.
 (7) When elemental mercury leaks on to an all-metallic structure, severe structural strength
 degradation can occur.
 (a) The rate of the diffusion of the mercury into a metal is related to the type of metal touched
 by the mercury

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 20-60-05-802-001 (Circuit Breaker Cycling).
resposta:
(1) This procedure is for on-the-ground maintenance and is preventative maintenance for those
 circuit breakers that are less frequently used. It is not necessary to do this procedure for
 frequently used circuit breakers. Because each airline operates differently, it is an airline
 decision as to which circuit breakers are frequently used and which circuit breakers are less
 frequently used.
 (2) Research has shown that the cycling of less frequently used circuit breakers can help to
 improve operational system reliability. If a circuit breaker has not been operated for some time,
 it is possible that the circuit breaker may not open when an electrical fault occurs.
 (3) Circuit breakers are located in all areas of the airplane such as the flight compartment,
 electrical equipment bays, cargo compartments, passenger compartment, and other areas.
 (4) Too much repeated use of a circuit breaker can result in premature failure of the circuit breaker.
SUBTASK 20-60-05-022-002

 (1) Do these steps to remove electrical power: PAGEBLOCK 24-22-00/201
 NOTE: Electrical power must be off so that subsequent incorrect fault indications or nuisance
 messages are prevented.

resposta:
(1) The Stall Warning System Test has these parts:
 (a) Preparation for Test
 (b) BITE Test
 (c) Stall Warning Operation Test
 (d) System Performance Test
 (e) Landing Gear Relay Test
 (f) Asymmetry Mode Test
 (g) High Thrust Mode Test
 (h) Speed Floor Test

RAM 001, 002; AIRPLANES WITH AIRSPEED TAPE DISPLAY AND WITH WINDSHEAR ALERT
 (i) Speed Tape and Pitch Limit Test
RAM 001, 002; AIRPLANES WITH DIGITAL STALL WARNING COMPUTERS
 (2) Specific values of engine N1 and N2 are necessary for the High Thrust Mode Test. There are
 two alternative procedures to supply these N1 and N2 values:
 (a) The first procedure is to supply a signal which is equivalent to the output of the N1 and
 N2 tachometer sensors. These sensors are located on the engines. For this procedure,
 you will connect the stall warning system tester and two function generators at the
 electrical connectors of the engine N1 and N2 sensors. To change the N1 or the N2
 value, you will change the frequency of the function generator output.
 (b) The second procedure is to supply a signal which is equivalent to the output of the N1

 within the high-stage regulator unit. The flow check mechanism is designed to shut off the

 valve which causes it to close in the event of a reverse flow condition.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 24-21-00-705-118 (Bus Transfer Interlock Test).
resposta:
(1) The purpose of this test is to check the integrity of the bus transfer interlocks provided by the
 auxiliary contacts of the Main Power Circuit Breakers. Transfer times of approximately 8 to 12
 milliseconds indicate correct behavior of the interlock and the integrity of the associated
 airplane wiring. Transfer times of approximately 4 milliseconds would indicate the loss of the
 appropriate interlock due to either 1. a malfunction of the auxiliary contact in the contactor
 being transferred FROM or 2. a short in the associated wiring which bypasses the auxiliary
 contact.
 This condition by itself would not result in paralleling sources but if coupled with a contactor
 slow to drop out by an additional 4 milliseconds or more, paralleling would be expected.
 (2) The test checks each phase during transfer thereby providing three checks of a particular type
 of transfer. If intermittent operation is suspected then wire wiggling at the contactor connectors
 in conjunction with the transfer test may be warranted.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 47-31-02-740-805 (BDU Fault History Menu).
resposta:
(1) This task gives the instructions to operate the BDU control panel for the Fault History Menu.
 (2) To help navigate through the NGS BDU fault history structure, refer to Figure 207.
 (3) The fault history menu allows you to look at NGS faults and correlated flight deck effects that
 occurred during the last 99 flight legs. The flight leg is updated during the ground to air (WOW)
 transition.
 (4) Fault history can store up to 256 messages. No more than 25% of the fault history can be
 allocated to a single flight leg. If a single flight leg fault allocation is full, no additional fault
 records can be recorded for that flight leg. When the total allocation of faults is full, new faults
 will replace the oldest fault.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 12-15-31-703-001 (Check Fluid Level by Pressure/Extension Method).
resposta:
(1) This procedure supplies instructions to check the level of the hydraulic fluid in the shock strut
 of the main landing gear.
 (a) To do a check of the fluid level, you must measure the pressure and the extension of the
 shock strut twice, at two different shock strut extensions. The greater the difference in the
 shock strut extension, the more accurate the fluid measurement will be.
 1) You can obtain the different shock strut extensions one of two ways:

RAM ALL 12-15-31

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 a) You can take the shock strut measurements at two different airplane weights,
 for example, before and after fueling the airplane, or,
 b) If the airplane is on jacks, you can use floor jacks or the airplane jacks to
 compress or extend the shock struts.
 2) You should have a difference of 2 -4 inches (50 - 100 mm) between the two shock
 strut extensions to do the check.
 3) There are no maximum strut extension allowable difference measurements between
 the left hand and right hand struts.
 4) The extension and pressure measurements for both the left hand and right hand
 struts must lie within the respective strut servicing bands for proper operation.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 51-21-41-370-801 (Apply Alodine 1132 Solution).
resposta:
SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-001

 (1) Remove the cap of the Alodine 1132 Coating, C50079, and hold the pen with the applicator tip
 downards.
 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-002

 (2) Activate the pen by pressing the applicator tip against a firm surface. This will open the valve
 allowing the premixed solution to flow to the applicator tip. A new pen should take 30 to 45
 seconds for the tip to be wet. When the tip is wet, release pressure. The pen is ready for use.
 SUBTASK 51-21-41-210-001

 (3) Ensure that surface to be coated is dry before proceeding.
 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-003

 (4) Apply Alodine 1132 coating to the part surface in smooth even strokes. Fifty percent overlap of
 strokes usually gives proper coating weight. Do not allow the Alodine 1132 to puddle. Puddling
 will increase the time required for drying, and thick uneven areas in the coating cause
 performance failures.
 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-004

 (5) Wait until coating dries and repeat the application in a cross hatch pattern. Do not water rinse.
 Water rinse degrades corrosion resistance and paint adhesion.
 SUBTASK 51-21-41-370-005

 (6) Ambient air dry or force air dry coating at 130°F maximum sufficiently to evaporate water.

resposta:
(1) When the DET SEL switch is set to A, and any detector in loop A detects smoke, an alarm will
 occur. Similarly, when the DET SEL switch is set to B, and B loop detects smoke, the alarm will
 occur.
 When the DET SEL switch is set to NORM, smoke must be detected in loop A and loop B (any
 detector in both loops, they do not have to be a pair) before the alarm will occur.
 NOTE: If you apply too much smoke to a detector, the excess smoke could affect adjacent
 detectors. Try to limit the amount of smoke applied to each detector.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 71-11-03-825-001-C00 (Fan Cowl Panel Lower Latch Adjustment).
resposta:
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to adjust the fan cowl lower latch.
 (2) You must adjust the fan cowl latches after a fan cowl panel is replaced. You must adjust the
 latches after a latch or keeper is replaced.
 (3) You must adjust the forward latch of the fan cowl panel after a fan cowl panel is replaced.
 (4) It can be necessary to adjust the fan cowl latches after the fan duct cowl and thrust reverser
 halves are replaced.
 (5) Three adjustments are given for the fan cowl panel lower latches:
 (a) The gap adjustment
 (b) The tension adjustment
 (c) The flushness adjustment.
 (6) The gap adjustment gives the correct clearance between the right and left cowl panels. The
 adjustment is made with shims at each latch location.

(1) The procedures in the maintenance manual are for light corrosion only. Refer to the Structural
 Repair Manual for heavy corrosion.

 airplane, use the applicable procedure to remove the corrosion.

 corrosion permits corrosion to start again.
 (5) If you cannot remove the light corrosion immediately, apply BMS 3-23 to help prevent more
 corrosion. Then you must remove the corrosion at the first available opportunity. BMS 3-23
 should not be used on surfaces where more than light corrosion is involved.

 necessary. Phosphoric acid type corrosion remover is weak and will not affect metal surfaces.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 34-12-01-710-802 (Air Data System - Operational Test (For Smith/GE ADC P/N 501FAD1-1)).
resposta:
(1) This is the air data system operational test for the Smith/GE Air Data Computer (ADC), part
 number 501FAD1-1.
 (2) The ADS operational test is a BITE test. The test operates from the controls on the front panel
 of the ADC. During the test, stable outputs are sent to the air data instruments and are
 monitored. The test makes sure of the conditions that follow:
 (a) The ADC electronics operate correctly.
 (b) The interface and warning system between the computer and instruments operate
 correctly.
 (c) The instruments operate when signals are sent to them.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 28-22-00-785-214 (Fuel Boost Pump Output Pressure Test).
resposta:
(1) This procedure does a check of the output pressure of each of the boost pumps in the No. 1
 tank and the No. 2 tank. If a pump does not supply a minimum output pressure, that pump
 could have a problem.
 (a) The output pressure can be measured two different ways:
 1) Method 1 measures the output pressure of each of the boost pumps at the drain for
 the fuel filter housing on one of the engines.
 2) Method 2 measures the output pressure of each of the boost pumps at the forward
 spar fitting for the fuel feed low pressure switch. This procedure is recommended if
 the low pressure switches are being replaced. Also, if one switch is to be replaced,
 all four switches are recommended to be replaced.
 (2) This test measures the output pressure of all four fuel boost pumps for the two main tanks.
 This test is not necessary for the two fuel boost pumps for the center fuel tank.
 (3) This procedure incorporates the output pressure test for the fuel boost pumps from Boeing
 Service Bulletin 737 28A1114R3.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 20-10-52-211-801 (CRES Hydraulic Hoses - Examination).
resposta:
(1) CRES hydraulic hoses can also be referred to as “Teflon Hoses.”
 (2) Teflon hoses are not subject to aging. The design objective for teflon hoses is that they are not
 life-limited.
 (3) Teflon is inert to contaminants found in aircraft applications. However, corrosive contaminants
 on a hose, particularly chlorine compounds, have resulted in corrosion pitting of the CRES wire
 braiding. Corrosion pitting of CRES hydraulic tubing has also been found in wheel wells and
 other areas. Periodic cleaning with a Boeing recommended cleaning solution
 (PAGEBLOCK 12-40-00/201), along with coating of the hoses with corrosion preventative
 compound or equivalent, could be beneficial.

(1) This task is for the removal of interior ice for these conditions:
 NOTE: This procedure will remove the ice build-up on the inside of the airplane structure.
 (a) Airplanes that have continuous operation in cold weather
 (b) Ice is found on interior equipment, furnishings, electrical components, wiring, control
 cables, pulleys, door mechanisms, or structure.
 (2) In the usual operation of the airplane, air comes through the airplane structure. During flight,
 the water vapor in the air can condense and freeze in the airplane. When you continuously
 operate the airplane in cold weather, ground temperatures below the freezing point will not let
 the ice melt. Too much ice will lower the performance of the airplane below the permitted
 values.

 System (EWIS)
 (a) Enhanced Zonal Analysis Procedure (EZAP) is an analytical procedure required by Part
 25, Appendix H, Section H25.5(a)(1) that identifies the physical and environmental
 conditions contained in each zone of an airplane, analyzes the effects of these conditions
 on electrical wiring and components, and assesses the possibilities for smoke and fire.
 The end result of the analysis are inspection and restoration tasks in the form of EWIS
 ICA.
 (b) Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS): means any wire, power feeder, wiring
 device, or combination of these, including termination devices, installed in any area of the
 airplane for the purpose of transmitting electrical energy, including data and signals,
 between two or more intended termination points. EWIS is defined in full by 14 CFR
 section 25.1701.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 05-51-57-212-040 (Volcanic Ash In-flight Encounter Conditional Inspection).
resposta:
(1) This inspection is divided into three phases (Phase I, Phase II and Phase III).
 (a) Phase I (IA and IB) is a general visual inspection for one or more of the following:
 1) The flight crew reported the airplane flight path was through a cloud of visual
 volcanic ash.
 2) The airplane lands or takes off in volcanic ash fallout conditions.
 NOTE: Fallout is identified as ash drifting down from the air, or is blown about by
 the wind. Fallout is also caused by the ash being blown or moved about
 because of the movement of airplanes and ramp vehicles.
 3) An airplane encounters volcanic ash while operating on the ground during volcanic
 ash fallout conditions.
 (b) Phase II is applicable when any of the Phase IB inspections show positive results.
 (c) Phase III is applicable when any of the Phase II inspections show positive results.
 (2) Volcanic ash has the qualities that follow:
 (a) It is hard and highly abrasive.
 (b) It usually contains trace chemicals which can be acidic (pH between 2 and neutral).
 (c) It can cause erosion/abrasion, etching or shot peening on exposed surfaces and remove
 protective finishes.
 (d) The dimensions of most ash particles are less than 5 microns

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 24-41-11-206-009 (External Power Receptacle Check).
resposta:
(1) If you use the External Power Receptacle in a dirty area too frequently, this will wear the
 receptacle pin and plug socket. This will cause too much heat and incorrect electrical
 connections.
 Corrosion or loose connections can also be the cause of the receptacle pins which become too
 hot. The connections are from the electrical conductors to the inner ends of the pins. Worn
 parts, too much heat and the result of the oxidation and corrosion will cause the pin and socket
 dimensions to change.
 (2) The external power receptacle contains four ac input pins that are 0.435 to 0.437 inch in the
 diameter. The receptacle also contains two dc control pins that are 0.310 to 0.312 inch in the
 diameter.
 The six pins are attached to a plastic base. The six pins have threads on the inboard ends, for
 the connection of the electrical cables. You cannot remove the pins for a replacement. Replace
 the damaged or smaller contact pins with a new support base which contains the six pins.

 pressure and relief valve.
 SUBTASK 21-32-11-024-011

 (2) Remove the relief valve door from the frame:
 (a) Remove the valve hinge bolts.
 (b) Disengage the spring from the frame anchor hole.
 NOTE: Do not permit the spring to move suddenly out of the frame anchor hole. Hold the
 spring while you lower it against the relief valve door.
 (c) Remove the relief valve door.
 SUBTASK 21-32-11-034-012

 (3) Remove the spring from the relief valve door:
 (a) Remove the fasteners which hold the spring support retainer to the relief valve door and
 remove the retainer.
 (b) Hold the spring while you remove the spring support rod.
 (c) Disengage the spring from the anchor hole in the relief valve door.
 NOTE: The spring will turn approximately 360°.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 51-00-53-102-109 (Corrosion Removal Procedures for Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium Alloys).
resposta:
(1) Stainless Steel and Nickel-Chromium Alloys are used where corrosion resistance is one of the
 major considerations in the design of a component or system.
 (2) In most applications these steels will have no other surface protection, except for matching
 color schemes of the surrounding structure or dissimilar metal organic coatings.
 (3) Stainless steel and nickel-chromium steels, however, are not free from corrosion attack.
 Corrosion will appear as pitting and will usually be black in color.
 (4) The existence of corrosion products prevents a passive environment at the stainless steel
 surfaces, and creates an active/passive corrosion cell (PAGEBLOCK 51-00-50/201). It is,
 therefore, necessary that any corrosion removal is done completely.

resposta:
(1) If the window is damaged as specified in this procedure, remove the window and replace or
 repair the damaged components (PAGEBLOCK 56-21-00/401).
 (2) Do the passenger cabin window inspection.
 (a) Crack:
 A crack is not a complete break but it has width when you look parallel to the face of the
 crack. A crack can occur at any angle to the surface of the prismatic pane. The direction
 of the crack depends on the direction of the applied force. The stress from a scratch or a
 craze can cause a crack to occur.
 (b) Crazing:
 A crazed prismatic pane has a number of very thin cracks which are 90 degrees to the
 surface of the prismatic pane. Because the cracks are very thin, it is not easy to see the
 crazing.
 When you look at the prismatic pane at different angles, you can see the crazing by its
 reflection on the smooth surface of the prismatic pane.
 (c) In-plane Cracking (delamination)
 In-plane cracking can be a smooth fissure, or group of fissures that can occur along the
 surface of the pane. In-plane cracks can occur in acrylic. The cracks start at the edges of
 the pane or in the center of the pane. You can best find the cracks with a reflection of light
 from the smoot

resposta:
(1) Software Installation Times
 (a) The time required to install software in a component is variable and is dependent on
 several factors that include:
 1) Retrieval of the correct software media, applicable equipment and Maintenance
 Manual procedure.
 2) Setup procedures.
 3) Data transfer time.
 4) Software configuration check.
 5) Return to usual airplane configuration.
 6) Airline completion procedures.
 (2) Data Transfer Times
 (a) The data transfer time is the actual time from disk or disks insertion into the data loader
 until the data transfer is complete.
 (b) The data transfer time depends on:
 1) The number of disks.
 2) The type and size of software files on each disk.
 3) The unique protocols and processors of the data loader.
 4) The unique internal protocols and processors of the component.
 5) Disks inserted in a timely manner.
 (c) Typical data transfer times are:
 1) Operational Program Software (OPS): approximately 5 to 16 minutes per disk; for
 example, if the OPS has four disks, then the complete installation can take as long
 as 64 minutes.
 2) Operational Program Configuration (OPC): approximately 1 to 3 minutes per disk.
 3) Databases: approximately 3 to 1

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 20-10-51-358-251 (Repair Hydraulic Tubing With Flexible Hoses).
resposta:
(1) The Boeing Company recommends that the operator do these procedures:
 (a) Make a record of the flexible hoses that you install as temporary repairs for rigid lines.

 20-10-51
 Page 898.2
 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (b) Make a schedule for the regular inspection of flexible hose installations. Make sure the
 installation stays an airworthy repair until the system is put back to its initial configuration.
 (c) Make a procedure to make sure the flexible hoses that are installed as temporary repairs
 are replaced as soon as possible. You must replace the hoses no later than the
 scheduled time check approved by the assigned principal maintenance inspector.
 (2) You can use many different repair techniques. The Boeing Company cannot know about or
 control these repair techniques. It is your responsibility to decide if this procedure is applicable
 to your repair techniques.
 (3) This procedure is not acceptable for engine hydraulic tube repair or for the replacement of rigid
 or flexible coiled tubing. Engine hydraulic tubes are those tubes below or forward of the
 firewall, and within the engine cowls. Consult Boeing when considering a repair to any engine
 hydraulic or coiled tube.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 12-15-41-703-014 (Examine the Fluid Level of the Shock Strut for the Nose Landing Gear).
resposta:
(1) This procedure supplies instructions to check the level of the hydraulic fluid in the shock strut
 of the main landing gear.
 (a) To do a check of the fluid level, you must measure the pressure and the extension of the
 shock strut twice, at two different shock strut extensions. The greater the difference in the
 shock strut extension, the more accurate the fluid measurement will be.
 1) You can obtain the different shock strut extensions one of two ways:
 a) You can take the shock strut measurements at two different airplane weights,
 for example, before and after fueling the airplane, or,
 b) If the airplane is on jacks, you can use floor jacks or the airplane jacks to
 compress or extend the shock struts.
 2) You should have a difference of 2 -4 inches (50 - 100 mm) between the two shock
 strut extensions to do the check.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 51-00-53-102-091 (Corrosion Removal Procedures for Carbon Steel).
resposta:
(1) Carbon steel, in its heated-treated form, is used in areas where high structural or aerodynamic
 loads occur on the airplane, for example:
 (a) Landing gear
 (b) Flap tracks
 (c) Structural splices
 (d) Terminal fittings and miscellaneous brackets

 51-00-53

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (e) Red 'iron' rust is one of the most familiar kinds of corrosion on carbon steel, and generally
 is caused by the formation of ferrous oxides due to atmospheric exposure.
 (f) Some surface metal oxides are purposely used to protect the underlying base metal.
 (g) Red 'iron' rust is not one of these, and actually attracts moisture from the air and
 promotes additional corrosion.
 (h) The red rust first shows on unprotected airplane hardware such as bolts, nuts and
 exposed fittings.
 (i) Slight corrosion damage on highly stressed steel parts can become potentially
 dangerous, and the so the rust must be removed and controlled.
 (j) Corroded steel parts should be removed from the airplane for treatment, if possible
 (k) The general procedures for the removal of corrosion are provided in the following
 paragraphs.

 the control cabin conditioned air distribution system (PAGEBLOCK 21-22-00/001 ).

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 80-11-01-205-001-C00 (Engine Starter Leak Check).
resposta:
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to do a leak check of the engine starter.
 (2) The intent of this task is to detect major oil leaks that are the result of a maintenance error,
 such as a missing or severely damaged O-ring on the starter output shaft.
 (3) It is recommended that operators carefully monitor the oil consumption on flights following
 starter installation. Do a high power engine run (>70 % N1) if the oil consumption shows a
 sudden increase.
 (4) It is recommended that the starter oil tank be re-serviced prior to conducting the idle leak check
 (TASK 12-13-41-603-001 and TASK 12-13-41-603-014). This will ensure maximum operational
 time in case of a small oil leak .

(1) These general instructions apply to the pitot-static system leak test.
 (a) The rate of the applied vacuum to a static system must be 5000 feet or less for each
 minute.
 (b) The release of the vacuum from a static system must be 5000 feet or less for each
 minute.
 (c) The rate of the applied pressure to a pitot system must be 300 knots or less for each
 minute.
 (d) The release of pressure from a pitot system must be 300 knots or less for each minute.
 (e) Absolute pressure in the pitot system must be equal or more than the pressure in the
 static system.
 (f) The differential pressure between the pitot and static systems must not be larger than
 10.00 inches of mercury.
 (g) The absolute pressure applied to a static system must not be more than ambient
 pressure when an instrument is connected to that static system.
 (h) The pressure in a static system must not be more than 32.10 inches of mercury.
 (i) Do not connect or disconnect equipment or indicators when you apply pressure or a
 vacuum to the pitot-static system.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 71-00-00-802-133-C00 (Power Plant (Cold Weather) Operation).
resposta:
(1) This procedure gives the instructions that are necessary to operate the engine during cold
 weather conditions. These instructions give the information, techniques, and additional
 procedures to supplement the usual operation procedure.
 (2) During cold weather operation, you can prevent damage to the engine if you do these steps:
 (a) Use the inlet cover and the exhaust cover.
 (b) Make sure the rotors are not locked before you start the engine.
 (c) You must prevent or remove the snow and ice that can collect around the inlet cowl.
 (3) Ice formation in the engine inlet is one of the principal hazards during cold weather engine
 operation.
 (a) Snow that is blown into a cooling engine can become ice if it melts and freezes again.
 1) This ice formation can lock the rotor blades to the stator case.
 2) This ice formation can cover the surface of the rotor blades and cause the blades to
 become unbalanced.
 (4) Rain and high winds that cause a large temperature decrease in a small amount of time can
 cause the ice to form in the engine and lock the rotors.
 (5) Ice formation during engine operation can occur because of the large airflows and the suction
 at the engine inlet.

(1) This task provides the instructions on how to examine the engine starter.

 necessary.

 for that minimum output pressure.

 Procedure 4B uses the built-in-test equipment in the Digital Flight Control System (DFCS
 BITE) to engage the autopilot actuators. If you do one of the procedures, it is not necessary for
 you to do the other.
 (2) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
 to find the internal leakage rate for each part. There are three procedures to measure the flow:
 the ammeter procedure, the flowmeter procedure, and the amp-clamp and multimeter
 procedure.

 lines connected. This may prevent the pumps from receiving enough hydraulic fluid
 from their respective reservoirs and cavitate the pump.

 motor on the electric motor-driven pump (EMDP). To find the flow you measure the
 current, subtract the applicable system basic current, and use Figure 603 to change it to

 flowmeter procedure, and the amp-clamp and multimeter procedure.

 motor on the standby EMDP. To find the flow you measure the current and use
 Figure 608 to change it to a flow.

 EMDP and read the flow from it.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 07-13-00-282-002 (Balance Check for the Tilted Airplane).
resposta:
(1) When you lift the airplane nose, the center of gravity of the airplane moves aft with respect to
 the main gear axle. This movement, plus the wind, upgrades, and fuel movement can cause
 the airplane to move. This can make the aft fuselage of the airplane touch the ground. Thus,
 you must complete a balance check form to make sure the airplane will be stable. Add the
 ballast, if it is necessary. You can use the dolly as a ballast. To do this, attach it to the nose
 gear wheels.
SUBTASK 07-13-00-972-022

 (1) Add the moments about the main gear due to these items:
 • Airplane weight (Figure 204)
 • Tilted airplane (Figure 205)
 • Fuel shift (Figure 206), wind (Figure 207)
 • Tow vehicle acceleration (Figure 208)
 • Upgrades (Figure 209)
 SUBTASK 07-13-00-972-023

 (2) Make sure the sum of these moments is more than +1,000,000 inch-pounds.

 07-13-00

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 SUBTASK 07-13-00-972-024

 (3) Make sure the dolly has the capacity equivalent to or more than the maximum load of the
 airplane nose (Figure 212).
 SUBTASK 07-13-00-972-025

 (4) Use Figure 213 as an example to do a balance check when you tow the airplane.

resposta:
SUBTASK 28-13-41-216-002

 (1) Do a check to see if the relief valve is open.
 (a) Find the access panel adjacent to the air vent scoop at the end of the wing (Figure 601).
 NOTE: This panel is not circular.
 (b) Find the poppet at the center of the access panel.

 NOTE: If the valve is open, the manual reset knob and its stem are below the poppet.

 (c) Slowly release the manual reset knob to make sure the poppet is locked in the closed
 position.
 (d) Continue to release the manual reset knob until the return spring retracts the reset knob
 into the opening.
 NOTE: The outer surface of the knob and the poppet must make a smooth surface with
 the airplane skin.

resposta:
(1) This task is the operational test procedure for the airborne vibration monitoring (AVM) system.

 (a) A self-test of the AVM signal conditioner.
 (b) A fault history check of the complete AVM system for faults external to the AVM signal
 conditioner from the recent flight(s).
 (c) An engine operation (one engine at idle) to check that the AVM system is operational.
 (3) You can use the operational test to make sure that the AVM signal conditioner operates after a
 component replacement.

resposta:
(1) This procedure gives instructions for making a structural repair to a fiberglass or Kevlar air
 conditioning duct.
 (2) A structural repair is applicable when the damage to the air conditioning duct is a cut or a hole
 that is more than 1/4 inch wide and more than 3 inches long but less than 5 percent of the total
 surface area of the duct. If the damage is more than 5 percent of the total surface area of the
 duct, replace the duct section.
 (3) This task includes steps to install insulation material on the air duct.
 (4) CFR 14 Part 121.312 mandates that insulation material installed in the fuselage as a
 replacement after September 2, 2005 must meet the flame propagation requirements of CFR
 Part 25.856, effective September 2, 2003.
 (5) Existing insulation material can be removed and re-installed if it is not damaged. Replacement
 insulation material must meet the flame propagation requirement.
 (6) Melamine foam insulation, G50449, BMS8-385, is the preferred foam insulation material that
 meets the flame propagation requirement.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 51-00-58-302-051 (Surface Treatment for Carbon Steels).
resposta:
(1) Bare surfaces of carbon (alloy) steels are highly reactive when exposed to the environment.
 Carbon steel is either cadmium or cadmiumtitanium plated after machining and heat treated.
 (2) Steel parts absorb hydrogen during processing operations and in service when hydrogen may
 be produced and diffused into the metal.
 Hydrogen absorption, can cause crack initiation and propagation, resulting in delayed brittle
 fracturing when the part is under sustained tensile strength.
 (3) The susceptibility of carbon steel parts to hydrogen embrittlement increases as hardness and
 strength increases.
 (4) Steel parts heat-treated to 180 ksi, and below, are not considered susceptible to hydrogen
 embrittlement, while steel parts heat- treated to 220 ksi, and above, are highly susceptible to
 hydrogen embrittlement and must be plated by low embrittlement processes.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 27-51-00-715-001 (Operational Test - Trailing Edge Flap System).
resposta:
(1) During the operational test, you make sure the operation of the trailing edge flaps is
 satisfactory. The test permits you to monitor the functions of the flap system on the ground with
 hydraulic power supplied by the engine-driven pumps or the ground power. The operational
 test does not make sure the flaps are adjusted correctly. You must not use this test as an
 alternate for the system test.
 (2) During the operational test you use the flap position indicators to find the flap positions. Thus,
 you must make sure the adjustment of the position indicator system for the trailing edge flaps
 is correct before you do the operational test.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 76-11-04-402-013-C00 (Engine Control Cables Installation).
resposta:
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to install the engine control cables.
 (2) The maintenance practices give the approximate location of the engine control cables in the
 fuselage, the wings and the strut.
 (a) This maintenance practice provides the lengths and fittings of the engine control cables.
 (b) The cable references are from end fitting to end fitting.
 (c) The T1A and T2A cables control the increase of the forward thrust.
 (d) The T1B and T2B cables control the decrease of the forward thrust.
 (e) The ESS1A and ESS2A cables control the engine start and the fuel to the run position.
 (f) The ESS1B and ESS2B cables control the engine shutdown and fuel to the cutoff
 position.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 52-09-10-350-802 (Seal Repair Procedure (Method B)).
resposta:
(1) This procedure is for repairs with an adhesive reinforced with open mesh fabric. The fabric is
 embedded in the adhesive on the seal surface.
SUBTASK 52-09-10-300-002

 (1) Do the steps that follow to repair the seal with adhesive and open-meshed fabric:
 (a) Cut the D117 Dacron Fabric, G00028 or P118 polyester fabric, G00029 to have the
 correct fit for the patch area.
 (b) Apply the adhesive to the repair area on the seal.
 (c) Push the fabric patch into the wet adhesive and apply more adhesive on top of the patch.
 (d) Make the surface smooth of unwanted adhesive and put a load on to make sure the seal
 fully touches the adhesive.
 (e) Apply pressure to make sure the parts are fully bonded.
 (f) Let the adhesive cure the minimum time necessary before you put a load on it.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 12-33-02-603-039 (Return the Airplane to Service After Cold Weather Unattended Parking at Temperatures Below).
resposta:
(1) This task is for airplanes after unattended parking when the temperatures of the interior and
 engines were not maintained above 32°F (0°C).
 (2) If the temperature has remained above -40°F (-40°C), passenger cabin warming is not
 necessary, but warming is required for the flight deck and EE bay.
 (3) For temperatures below 5°F (-15°C), the EE bay must be warmed before the electronics are
 energized.
 (4) For temperatures below -4°F (-20°C), the flight deck must be warmed before the electronics
 are energized.

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 22-31-00-715-056 (Operational Test - Autothrottle System).
resposta:
(1) The operational test does a fast check on the autothrottle system. This test uses some of the
 A/T BITE tests. The A/T BITE can be done step by step on the FMCS control display unit
 (CDU). For instruction on how to use the A/T BITE, refer to AUTOTHROTTLE SYSTEM -
 BUILT-IN TEST EQUIPMENT, SECTION 22-04, A/T system - Built-In Test Equipment.
 (2) The CDU data lines are identified with a caret (<) or (>) adjacent to the line-select key (LSK).
 The two terms used for page/sequence control of the BITE are: CONTINUE> and <INDEX.
 CONTINUE> lets you continue to the next page of the procedure. <INDEX lets you go back to
 the previous index page.
 (3) The FMCS CDU (Figure 501) has 12 LSK (6 on each side of the CDU display). These keys are
 identified as 1L to 6L and 1R to 6R. If a step shows "LSK 6L", it refers to the sixth key down on
 the left hand side of the CDU display.
