(1) This procedure is a test for the correct operation of these valves:
 (a) The removal valve for each of the boost pumps
 (b) The discharge check valve for each of the boost pumps

RAM 001-006, 501-504 PRE SB 737-28-1100
 (c) The redundant check valve for the aft boost pumps.
 (d) The forward/center redundant check valves for the forward boost pumps in the main tank
 and the boost pumps in the center tank.

 (e) The vent valve for each of the boost pumps in the No. 1 tank and the No. 2 tank.
 (f) The check valve for the fueling line outlet on each of the boost pumps in the center tank.
 (2) It is frequently not easy to find the valve that does not operate correctly. This is because all
 these valves let leakage go out of the same drain valve if they have leakage. It is a good
 procedure to do the test of the discharge check valve for the fuel boost pump first. This is
 because you can isolate it from the other valves, but you can not isolate it fully. If you find the
 discharge check valve for the fuel boost pump operates correctly, you must make a decision to
 replace one of these valves:
 (a) the removal valve
 (b) the vent valve

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 72-00-00-290-801-C00 (High Pressure Turbine (HPT) Blades Inspection).
resposta:
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to examine the HPT blades.
 (2) This inspection has two procedures: the first inspection uses the rigid borescope and the
 second inspection uses the flexible borescope.
 (a) The first inspection examines the HPT blades except the leading edges.
 (b) The first inspection can be accomplished at either the S17 or S18 borescope port. It is
 necessary to turn the N2 rotor to examine the HPT blades.
 (c) The second inspection examines the HPT blades and shrouds.
 (d) The second inspection begins at the left spark igniter port. It is necessary to turn the N2
 rotor to examine the HPT blades.
 (e) The inspection of the HPT shrouds is done again at the right igniter port.
 (3) You will do an inspection of the leading edges of the HPT blades with a flexible borescope if
 you find damage to the HPT blade during an inspection with a rigid borescope. You will also do
 the inspection if you think there is damage to the leading edge.
 (4) Do an inspection of the leading edge of the HPT blade after EGT temperatures above 955° C.

resposta:

resposta:
(1) Use this procedure with TRT ERT-530(A) receiver/transmitters (R/Ts) that have digital radio
 altitude output.
SUBTASK 34-48-02-720-006

 (1) Do the steps below to make a check of the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922 ramp-down
 program:
 (a) Push the RAMP/HOLD key on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922.
 1) Make sure the RAMPING light comes on.
 (b) Look for these conditions on the applicable EADI radio altitude display.
 1) The display is blank for approximately 75 seconds after you push the REMOTE
 TEST-START button.
 2) The display then shows 2500 (white numerals) and decreases at 20 fps (feet per
 second).
 3) After approximately 52 seconds, the display on the captain's and first officer's PFD
 are as follows:
 a) The letters DH will flash (amber) for three seconds on the captain's PFD.
 b) The letters DH will flash (amber) for three seconds on the first officer's PFD.
 4) The radio altitude continues to decrease to the stop altitude of -20 feet.

 structural component for pressure fail-safety and bird impact resistance.
 4) Laminate: Assembly of interlayer materials and glass panes bonded together by
 application of heat and pressure.
 5) Metal Insert: A thin piece of metal around the periphery of the window used to
 transfer failsafe pressure or bird impact loads from the interlayer to the window
 installation fasteners.
 6) Pane: One layer of glass or acrylic in a window.
 7) Pressure Seal: A rubber gasket that makes a pressure seal between the window

 (2) Phosphate treatments on a metal surface provides a good adhesion surface for organic
 finishes, and provides good wear and corrosion resistance when used with oil or corrosion
 preventive compounds.
 (3) Cadmium plating corrosion will appear as a dull gray product.
 (4) Phosphate treated surfaces will appear as a red-black part, darker than common rust, when
 corroded.

resposta:
(1) This procedure is an Enhanced Zonal Analysis Procedure (EZAP) task.
 (2) This procedure performs a detailed inspection of Electrical Wiring Interconnection System
 (EWIS).

 detailed inspection of exposed Fuel Quantity Indicating System (FQIS) EWIS inside a fuel
 tank.

 (1) Electrical Wiring Interconnection System (EWIS): means any wire, power feeder, wiring device,
 or combination of these, including termination devices, installed in any area of the airplane for
 the purpose of transmitting electrical energy, including data and signals, between two or more
 intended termination points. EWIS is defined in full by 14 CFR section 25.1701.
 (2) Detailed Inspection (DET)—An intensive examination of a specific item, installation, or
 assembly to detect damage, failure, or irregularity. Available lighting is normally supplemented
 with a direct source of good lighting at an intensity deemed appropriate. Inspection aids such
 as mirrors, magnifying lenses, or other means may be necessary. Surface cleaning and

 surface of the tank is usually the point where the leak path goes through the seal plane. But if

 find the correct point where the leak path goes through the seal plane and repair it. Thus it is

pergunta: Descreva o procedimento da task 73-11-02-308-007-C00 (Defective D-Bolts On The Main Fuel Filter Housing Replacement).
resposta:
(1) This procedure is to be done when D-bolts on the main fuel filter housing are found to be
 damaged.
SUBTASK 73-11-02-028-008-C00

 (1) Remove the fuel filter cover (TASK 73-21-02-004-001-C00):
 (a) Put a 1 gal. plastic container, STD-206 below the engine to collect residual fuel that
 drains out.
 (b) Cut and remove the lockwire from the drain plug.
 (c) Remove the drain plug and let the fuel drain.
 (d) Remove and discard the O-ring from the drain plug.
 (e) Remove the hex-head bolt and the washer.
 (f) Remove the five nuts and five flat washers from the fuel filter cover.
 1) Discard the nut and flat washer of the defective or damaged D-bolt.
 (g) Remove the fuel filter cover.
 (h) Remove and discard the O-ring from the fuel filter cover.
 SUBTASK 73-11-02-968-009-C00

 (2) Replace the D-bolts from the main fuel pump housing:
 (a) Remove and discard the retaining ring.
 (b) Remove and discard the damaged or defective D-bolt.
 (c) Install a new D-bolt on the main fuel pump housing.
 (d) Install a new retaining ring on the D-bolt.
 SUBTASK 73-11-02-428-010-C00

 (3) Install the fuel filter cover (TASK 73-21-02-404-010-C00).
